notable_absence.finding: This page directly TENSIONS the already-promoted relation service:query-service exemptFromMemoryQuota (stated elsewhere in the corpus as 'The Query and Backup services are exceptions and do not require a memory quota'). This page's own Memory Quotas panel lists a Query field ('The soft memory limit for every Query node in the cluster... When set to 0 (the default), there is no soft memory limit') alongside the other five services' quotas, described in parallel language. The reconciling reading is that Query is exempt from a MANDATORY/hard quota but still exposes an OPTIONAL soft one - the two statements are not strictly contradictory - but no page states this reconciliation explicitly, and a reader of this page alone, without the other promoted relation, would conclude Query's memory allocation works exactly like Data/Index/Search/Analytics/Eventing's. Flagged for reconciliation rather than resolved here.

cross_component_finding: The Node Availability panel's Ephemeral-bucket-only subsection (auto-reprovisioning; auto-failover for no-replica ephemeral buckets) is a NEW SHAPE of type-gated capability not seen elsewhere in this batch: earlier pages showed bucket type gating WHICH VALUES a shared setting can take (durability, ejection) or WHETHER a setting applies at all (auto-compaction, storage backend, encryption at rest). This page instead shows bucket type creating ENTIRE CLUSTER-WIDE RECOVERY MECHANISMS THAT ONLY EXIST for one type - auto-reprovisioning has no Couchbase-bucket equivalent at all, because a Couchbase bucket's data survives a node restart on disk and never needs replica-promotion to avoid loss. This is the clearest evidence yet that bucket type is a genuinely load-bearing, product-level axis rather than a per-setting detail.
